key_insight: STAR-XPC uses a permutation-invariant Set Transformer to predict X-ray transmission through polymer composites in milliseconds with high agreement to Monte Carlo simulations.
engineering_relevance: Fast transmission estimates could accelerate screening of polyethylene-based radiation-shielding composites within the studied operating range.
method: Embed molecular constituents with pretrained ChemBERTa.
Combine unordered constituent embeddings, mass fractions, and four bulk physical descriptors using a Set Transformer.
Train on automated PENELOPE/penEasy simulations for 30–120 kV sources and 0.15–2.5 mm slabs.
evidence_signal: On 4,697 simulated configurations, leakage-free, jointly stratified 10-fold cross-validation achieved R² = 0.9988, MSE = (1.12 ± 0.56) × 10⁻⁴, and median absolute percentage error of 1.15%.
watch_item: Validation is simulation-based; performance on experimental measurements, unfamiliar chemistries, or conditions outside the studied range remains unestablished.
paper_title: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
